_meta.honest_yield_note: 1 confirmed note is the correct result for an epic adventure text vs. gnomic Upaniṣadic prose. The single note (māyā V.34.14 ↔ Śvet.Up 1.10; 4.10; BṛhUp 2.5.19) is justified because Rāvaṇa explicitly called māyāvī in a philosophically loaded context. All other stems are either: (a) ātman used as reflexive pronoun in Sundara (not philosophical Self); (b) karma used in the physical sense 'action' not 'karmic retribution'; (c) terms where no Sundara verse invokes the philosophical sense.

rejected.sund: 51 occurrences (ātmānam = himself; mahātmā = great-souled; samīkṣitātmā = self-examining)
rejected.reason: In all 51 Sundara occurrences, ātman functions as reflexive pronoun ('himself', 'itself') or as honorific prefix (mahātmā = great-souled hero). None invoke the Upaniṣadic Absolute Self (brahma = ātmā). The philosophical sense has not yet crystallized as a self-standing concept in the epic. Reject as category error.

Karma in Sundara = 'deed/action/task' (kārya, duṣkara karma etc.) — consistently in the physical, not soteriological, sense. The Upaniṣadic use (karmic retribution, saṃsāra) does not illuminate any specific Sundara verse. Too generic. Reject.

Mokṣa in Sundara = 'release, escape' (śramaṃ mokṣaya = 'relieve your fatigue'; vimokṣyase = 'you will not escape'). Not the soteriological liberation of Upaniṣadic mokṣa. False cognate in different registers. Reject.

Prāṇa in Sundara = literal breath/life-breath, not cosmic life-force or Brahman-as-prāṇa. BṛhUp 4.1.3 defines prāṇa as 'highest Brahman' — this philosophical elevation is Upaniṣadic, not Sundara's. Register mismatch. Reject.

Satya in Sundara = truthfulness, sworn word, promise (satyaṃ pratiśṛṇomi = 'I truly promise'). Covered by the dharmashastra cluster (Manu 4.138). The Upaniṣadic satya (Taittirīya 2.1: satyaṃ jñānam anantaṃ brahma) is a different, higher metaphysical sense not invoked in Sundara. Reject as duplicate (better parallel already in dharmashastra cluster).

Tapas in BṛhUp 1.5.1 (medhayā tapasā janayat) = cosmic creative power. Sundara uses tapas in the standard epic sense (austerity practice). The overlap is real but too general for a note: tapas as austerity pervades all Sanskrit literature and does not require Upaniṣadic citation. Reject.

Sundara V.51.40 context: devāsura-narendreṣu … gandharveṣu mṛgeṣu ca — this is a list of beings (verse does not contain akṣara at all in the SLP1 text; the stem hit is a false positive on some other word). Even if present, the Upaniṣadic akṣara (= Absolute Imperishable, BṛhUp 3.8.8) would be unrelated to a list of celestial beings. Reject as false positive.

Sundara V.1.179: 'the sky fashioned by Brahman (brahmanirmite)' — brahman here = the creator god Brahmā (masculine), not brahman the neuter Absolute of Upaniṣads. KaṭhUp 1.1.9 uses brahman in address to a Brahmin guest (brahmann atithir). MuṇḍUp 3.2.10 uses brahman in the sense of Sacred Knowledge. None of these illuminate V.1.179's 'sky fashioned by Brahmā the god'. Reject as category mismatch (masculine vs. neuter brahman).
